newsitem.title: USA: AFTER THE BELL - Tobacco stocks settle after pact.
newsitem.headline: AFTER THE BELL - Tobacco stocks settle after pact.

text.p: Tobacco stocks continued to gyrate after the bell Friday, but eventually traded in line with closing prices as the smoke cleared around a landmark agreement between the tobacco industry and state attorneys general.
Philip Morris was at 45-5/8 in after-hours trading, flat with its closing price, although the tobacco company's stock dipped to 45 soon after the U.S market close.
Dealers said RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp traded at 34-1/2, also matching its closing price, although the stock rose to 34-5/8 soon after the close of regular trading.
"They're moving in," a trader said of tobacco stocks' shift toward closing prices.

The agreement, announced late Friday afternoon, would require tobacco companies to pay $368.5 billion over 25 years to compensate states and smokers for medical treatment and other smoking-related costs.
It also calls for curbs on the marketing of cigarettes to children, including a ban on cigarette vending machines.
During regular hours trading, Philip Morris and RJR Nabisco lost 2-1/8 and 1-1/8 points, respectively.
Other stocks remained in line with closing prices. "The tobacco's really the only thing that's exciting," a trader said.
Registering just a small gain, Regis Corp rose 1/4 to trade at 24-1/4 after announcing it had agreed to settle a lawsuit with the former chief executive of its Supercuts subsidiary, David Lipson.
Lipson was dismissed by Supercuts directors in January, 1996, the company said.
The New York Stock Exchange said session one volume rose to 64,500, up from Thursday's 5,300, while session two volume also rose to 308,300 from the previous day's 265,319.
AMEX, meanwhile, reported that 50,000 shares were traded after-hours, compared with 25,900 on Thursday.
